summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via a femoral catheter, HIV/AIDS, and a history of MRSA bacteremia was admitted for positive blood cultures and purulent drainage from her left femoral dialysis catheter. She was diagnosed with MRSA bacteremia likely originating from the catheter. The infected catheter was removed, and after a brief line holiday, a new right femoral tunneled catheter was placed. During the admission, she developed hyperkalemia requiring emergent dialysis. An IVC stent was placed to address chronic stenosis contributing to access complications and hypotension. She completed a course of vancomycin, with surveillance cultures turning negative. Her HIV was noted to be poorly controlled with a high viral load and low CD4 count, and she was encouraged to improve adherence. She was discharged to an extended care facility to complete her antibiotic course with plans for follow-up on anticoagulation, HIV management, and mental health support.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
